findings.description: Non-ratifier list inconsistent with icescr-at-fifty.md. Template letters list 'Comoros, Cuba, Palau, and Andorra' as signatories that never completed ratification (lines 39, 165). icescr-at-fifty.md line 56 lists 'Cuba, Palau, Nauru, and Comoros' as notable non-ratifiers. One list includes Andorra, the other includes Nauru. Both lists omit the other's member. Cross-page factual inconsistency undermines credibility.
findings.suggestion: Reconcile the two lists. Either enumerate the same states in both locations, or make the signatory vs. non-ratifier distinction explicit (signatories who signed but never ratified vs. states that never signed at all). Verify each state's actual status against the UN Treaty Collection.
findings.context: Template letter: 'The United States remains in the company of Comoros, Cuba, Palau, and Andorra among signatories that never completed ratification.' icescr-at-fifty: 'The remaining notable states that have not ratified include Cuba (which signed in 2008), several small island nations (Palau and Nauru), and Comoros.'

findings.description: 550,000 jobs figure stated as accomplished fact rather than projection. 'Shedding 550,000 jobs without a government strategy' treats a projection as current reality. why-act.mdx line 19 properly hedges the same figure as 'projected.' template-letters.mdx line 91 also properly uses 'project.' The talking-points formulation drops the hedging.
findings.suggestion: Change 'Shedding 550,000 jobs' to 'Projected loss of 550,000 jobs' or 'A projected 550,000 fewer jobs' to match the hedged language used elsewhere on the site. Add the source attribution (the figure appears to derive from tariff-effect modeling but lacks a citation in all three locations).
findings.context: talking-points: 'Shedding 550,000 jobs without a government strategy to absorb the displacement should alarm every constituent.' why-act: '550,000 fewer jobs projected from tariff effects alone.'

findings.description: BLS Displaced Workers data cited as domestic polling. Under the heading 'Domestic Polling on Economic Rights,' the third bullet cites bls.gov/news.release/disp.nr0.htm as evidence that 'Workers across the political spectrum support job transition assistance programs.' The BLS Displaced Workers Summary reports statistical data on worker displacement, not polling data on public support for transition programs. The source does not support the claim as framed.
findings.suggestion: Either replace the BLS link with an actual polling source that measures public support for job transition assistance (e.g., Pew Research workforce survey data), or move this bullet outside the 'Domestic Polling' section and reframe it as labor market evidence rather than opinion polling.
findings.context: Section header: 'Domestic Polling on Economic Rights.' Bullet: 'Workers across the political spectrum support [job transition assistance](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/disp.nr0.htm) programs during economic disruption.'

findings.description: Comoros ratification status flagged as 'pending verification' within the same paragraph that asserts '173 countries have ratified' without qualification. The uncertainty about Comoros's status does not propagate to the headline count. If Comoros has not ratified, the count would differ.
findings.suggestion: Add a brief qualifier: '173 countries have ratified the ICESCR (pending verification of one signatory's status)' or resolve Comoros's status against the UN Treaty Collection and remove the parenthetical uncertainty.
findings.context: 'As of 2026, 173 countries have ratified the ICESCR. [...] Comoros (signed 2008, ratification status pending verification).'

epistemic_flags: Non-ratifier lists compared across site pages without verifying against the UN Treaty Collection directly — psychology-agent relied on the content as written rather than primary source verification.
550,000 jobs figure source not independently verified — flagged for inconsistent hedging only.
